Crispy Sesame Shrimp and Beef: Calories, Reviews and Availability

ByShaziaa October 18, 2026October 18, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:53
Instaread

Panda Express Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef is a limited-time surf-and-turf entrée launched nationwide October 8, 2025, combining tempura shrimp and crispy beef strips in a sesame-chili sauce. It contains 410 calories per 5.6 oz serving. Reviews are mixed: the beef impresses, but the shrimp batter softens quickly once sauced.

Fast Food Menu

What Is Panda Express Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef?

Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef is a limited-time offer (LTO) that debuted nationwide on October 8, 2025. According to Panda  Restaurant Group’s press release (PandaRG.com, Oct. 6, 2025), it pairs tempura-battered shrimp with crispy beef strips, bell peppers, and green beans in a sesame-forward sauce inspired by the Sichuan dish Mouthwatering Chicken.

Discover more
Nutrition Guide
Family Meal Deals
Restaurant Locator

Panda Express Executive Chef Jimmy Wang described the entrée as a reworking of ingredients fans already know from Honey Walnut Shrimp and Beijing Beef, “coated in punchy, aromatic flavors and packed with layered textures” (PandaRG.com, Oct. 6, 2025). The launch coincided with “Wok Wednesdays,” a gamified feature inside the Panda Rewards app that lets members unlock same-day reward offers.

Fast Food Menu

No official end date for the LTO has been published. As of this writing (October 2026), availability should be confirmed in the Panda Express app or at your local  restaurant, since LTOs can wind down with little notice.

What Does Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef Taste Like?

The dish delivers a sticky, sweet-and-spicy sesame glaze over crisp-fried shrimp and beef, with crunchy green beans and red bell peppers for contrast. Tasting Table (Oct. 10, 2025) called the sauce “thick like a glaze” with “subtle sesame undertones” and “decidedly fiery” heat from dried  Chinese chili peppers.

The LTO Digest’s reviewer summed it up directly: “The beef is the standout. Lightly battered, still semi-crisp, and the sesame glaze suits it better than Beijing Beef’s usual ultra-sweet sauce.” The same review noted a weakness: “The shrimp struggles… First bite is fine. Third bite becomes soft and uniform.”

Delivery Service

Spice level is debated. Fast Food Post described the sauce as “mildly spicy,” while Reddit users in r/PandaExpress reported it ran “way too hot” and “super spicy and super salty.” The LTO Digest called it “legitimately spicy” for Panda but “a gentle medium” by general standards. Order it fresh from a recently refilled pan if you want the crispiest texture  a thin, sitting batch softens faster, especially on the shrimp.

How Many Calories Are in Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef?

A 5.6 oz serving of Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef contains 410 calories, 4g saturated fat (20% DV), 36g carbohydrates (12% DV), and 15g protein (30% DV), according to Panda Express nutrition data reported by fastfoodnutrition.org (updated 10/9/2025).

Total fat and sodium figures were not published at launch, so we won’t guess at them here. Allergen data lists gluten, sesame, shellfish, soy, and wheat as present; egg, fish, milk, peanuts, and tree nuts are not listed, though Panda notes shared equipment can’t guarantee any item is fully allergen-free.

For context, Beijing Beef comes in at 480 calories for the same 5.6 oz portion, per Panda Express nutrition data, making the new LTO 70 calories lighter at an equal serving size.

Fast Food Menu

Why Did Panda Express Launch This as a Limited-Time Item?

Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef follows Panda’s established “surf and turf” LTO playbook: combine two proven, already-in-supply proteins with one new sauce. This keeps kitchen complexity low while giving the menu a fresh seasonal hook.

Order Fast Food

The LTO Digest’s analysis frames this as a deliberate pattern: Panda, still privately owned by the Cherng family, “tends to improve its menu slowly, deliberately, and internally” rather than reactively. The reviewer notes the dish is “a smart remix using Panda’s existing supply chain and proven components”  reusing Beijing Beef’s beef prep and Honey Walnut Shrimp’s shrimp batter rather than developing new proteins from scratch.

This mirrors prior Panda premium LTOs. Chili Crisp Shrimp launched nationwide in September 2023, and Buldak Dynamite Sweet & Sour Chicken ran nationwide from March 9 to May 25, 2026. Premium shrimp and steak items typically carry a $1.50 upcharge, consistent with this entrée’s pricing.

Will Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef Come Back?

Panda Express has not announced an official return date or confirmed the item is leaving permanently. Because the dish reuses existing beef and shrimp supply chains, bringing it back would require minimal new sourcing  a factor that could favor a future re-release, though this is analysis, not a confirmed plan.

Fast Food Menu

The LTO Digest’s reviewer suggested the sauce itself “is worth re-exploring in future LTOs,” and floated interest in a beef-only version without the shrimp, which struggled to hold its crisp texture under the sauce. Until Panda issues an official statement, treat any return timeline as speculation.

What Are the Best Current-Menu Alternatives?

If Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef isn’t available near you, Beijing Beef covers the crispy-beef craving, Honey Walnut Shrimp covers the shrimp craving, Typhoon Chili Shrimp offers a similar spicy-shrimp profile (where available), and Black Pepper Sirloin Steak is the lighter-calorie protein option.

Choose Beijing Beef if you want the crispy-beef texture without shrimp. Choose Honey Walnut Shrimp if the candied walnut sweetness matters more than spice. Choose Black Pepper Sirloin Steak if calorie count is your priority. Typhoon Chili Shrimp was a test item available at roughly 20  restaurants across California, Los Angeles, and Texas through September 7, 2026, so confirm current availability in the Panda Express app before counting on it, since its test window has technically closed and its nutrition figures remain unofficial.

What Are Reviewers Saying About Panda Express Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef?

Professional reviewers generally praised the beef and sauce while flagging the shrimp’s texture. Tasting Table called the dish “amazing” overall, while The LTO Digest rated it “worth trying once,” and Reddit users reported inconsistent spice and saltiness.

Tasting Table’s Robin Miller (Oct. 10, 2025) wrote: “I can sum up my impression of the Panda Express Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef in one word: amazing,” adding that the portion size felt appropriate “for a price point of about $11.”

Frequently Asked Questions

How many calories are in Panda Express Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef?
A 5.6 oz serving contains 410 calories, according to Panda Express data reported by fastfoodnutrition.org (updated 10/9/2025).

How much does Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef cost?
Per Fast  Food Post, pricing starts around $10 for the entrée upcharge, with a Plate at $13.10 and a Bigger Plate at $16.20, though prices vary by location.

When did Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef launch?
It launched nationwide on October 8, 2025, according to Panda  Restaurant Group’s press release.

Order Fast Food

Does Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef contain shellfish?
Yes. Listed allergens include gluten, sesame, shellfish, soy, and wheat, per fastfoodnutrition.org.

Is Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef spicy?
Reports vary: Fast Food Post called it “mildly spicy,” while The LTO Digest and Reddit users described it as noticeably hotter, sometimes “way too hot.”

How does it compare to Beijing Beef in calories?
It has 410 calories versus Beijing Beef’s 480 calories for the same 5.6 oz portion, a 70-calorie difference.

Is there an upcharge for this entrée?
Yes, a $1.50 premium upcharge applies, consistent with Panda’s standard pricing for shrimp and steak entrées.

Will Crispy Sesame Shrimp & Beef return after it’s gone?
No official return date has been announced; its reuse of existing supply components makes a future comeback plausible but unconfirmed.

What percentage of reviewers think it’s healthy?
In an informal fastfoodnutrition.org poll, 75% of voters (6 of 8) said they consider it healthy.

What’s the protein content per serving?
It contains 15g of protein per 5.6 oz serving, or 30% of the daily value based on a 2,000-calorie diet.
